key_insight: A video autoencoder shapes both the computational cost of a world model and how quickly actions affect its predictions. Autoencoders designed for offline video generation may therefore be poor defaults for interactive simulation.
problem_solved: Interactive world models need efficient frame prediction and responsive action feedback, but often reuse autoencoders built for text-to-video generation, where no agent is waiting for a response.
method: Reassess video autoencoder design around the requirements of action-conditioned, interactive world models.
Examine how latent compression determines per-frame computation and action-response delay.
The supplied abstract is truncated; specific architectures, experiments, and results are not available.
impact: For practitioners building AI simulators, the autoencoder is a systems-level choice—not just a compression component. Prioritizing interaction latency alongside computational efficiency could make world models more useful for agent training, planning, evaluation, and human control.

paper_title: Rethinking Video Autoencoders for Interactive World Models
paper_authors: Adrien Ramanana Rahary, Yutong Bai, Nicolas Dufour, Patrick Pérez, David Picard
